newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank-Waigel plans changes to its accounts.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank-Waigel plans changes to its accounts.

text.p: The Bundesbank said that at a meeting on Thursday Finance Minister Theo Waigel had presented initial thoughts on changes to the accounting methods used by the central bank.

A statement issued by the Bundesbank gave no comment on the details of Waigel's plan. Government sources have said one plan was to consider a revaluation of the central bank's gold, which is currently in its books at well below market value.

Amid market speculation that the real aim of Waigel's plans is to drum up funds for Bonn's budget coffers, the Bundesbank presented the plans simply as a change to put the central bank's books in order ahead of the start of monetary union.

"With respect to the principles envisioned for accounting within the European System of Central Banks, Finance Minister Theo Waigel and State Secretary Juergen Stark presented initial thoughts on changes to some definitions on accounting principles in the Bundesbank law and conducted an initial exchange of views with the members of the central bank council at the meeting," the statement said.
"The central bank council's discussions will be continued soon on the basis of a draft paper which will be drawn up by the German Finance Ministry," the statement added.
The statement gave no further details.
